blue-moon-l.text: Once in a blue moon. Very rarely.

break-bank-l.text: Break the bank. To cost too much money.

break-ice-l.text: Break the ice. To make people feel relaxed when they first meet.

break-news-l.text: Break the news. To tell someone important, often bad, news.

butterflies-e.text: I always get butterflies in my stomach before a presentation.

butterflies-l.text: Butterflies in your stomach. A nervous feeling before something important.

by-ear-e.text: We don't know how busy it'll be, so let's play it by ear.

cat-bag-l.text: Let the cat out of the bag. To tell a secret by mistake.

chin-up-e.text: Keep your chin up — the worst part is over.

chin-up-l.text: Keep your chin up. Stay positive in a difficult situation.

clean-bill-e.text: After the tests, the cardiologist gave him a clean bill of health.

clean-bill-l.text: A clean bill of health. A report that someone is healthy or something is in good condition.

cold-feet-e.text: He got cold feet the night before the operation.

cold-feet-l.text: Get cold feet. To suddenly feel too nervous to do something you planned.

cut-chase-e.text: Let me cut to the chase: we need two more nurses.

cut-chase-l.text: Cut to the chase. To talk about the most important thing immediately.

cut-corners-e.text: Never cut corners with sterile technique.

cut-corners-l.text: Cut corners. To do something quickly or cheaply by ignoring rules or quality.

drawing-board-e.text: The pilot project failed, so it's back to the drawing board.

drawing-board-l.text: Back to the drawing board. To start again because a plan has failed.

easier-said-e.text: Just get more sleep, he said. That's easier said than done on night shifts.

easier-said-l.text: Easier said than done. It sounds easy, but it is hard to do.

ends-meet-e.text: Many junior doctors struggle to make ends meet.

ends-meet-l.text: Make ends meet. To have just enough money for basic things.

extra-mile-e.text: The nurses on this ward go the extra mile for every patient.

extra-mile-l.text: Go the extra mile. To make more effort than is expected.

eye-to-eye-e.text: Surgeons and neurologists don't always see eye to eye.

eye-to-eye-l.text: See eye to eye. To agree with someone.

fit-fiddle-e.text: At eighty, my grandfather is still as fit as a fiddle.

fit-fiddle-l.text: As fit as a fiddle. Very healthy and strong.

from-scratch-e.text: We had to rewrite the protocol from scratch.

from-scratch-l.text: From scratch. From the very beginning, without using anything done before.

hot-water-e.text: He'll be in hot water if he misses another deadline.

hot-water-l.text: In hot water. In trouble, especially with someone in authority.

house-fire-a.text: Get on like a house on fire.

house-fire-e.text: My mum and my wife got on like a house on fire.

house-fire-l.text: Get on like a house on fire. To like each other and become friends very quickly.

last-straw-e.text: The third night call in a row was the last straw.

last-straw-l.text: The last straw. The last of several bad things that makes you lose patience.

learn-ropes-e.text: It took me a month to learn the ropes in the new unit.

learn-ropes-l.text: Learn the ropes. To learn how to do a job.

long-run-e.text: In the long run, prevention is cheaper than treatment.

long-run-l.text: In the long run. Over a long period of time; in the end.

long-shot-e.text: It's a long shot, but the new trial might accept him.

long-shot-l.text: A long shot. An attempt that is unlikely to succeed.

make-up-mind-e.text: She couldn't make up her mind about the surgery.

make-up-mind-l.text: Make up your mind. To decide.

midnight-oil-e.text: I've been burning the midnight oil to finish the paper.

midnight-oil-l.text: Burn the midnight oil. To work or study late at night.

money-trees-l.text: Money doesn't grow on trees. Money is limited, so you should not waste it.

nail-head-a.text: Hit the nail on the head.

nail-head-l.text: Hit the nail on the head. To describe exactly what is causing a problem.

nick-of-time-e.text: The ambulance arrived in the nick of time.

nick-of-time-l.text: In the nick of time. At the last possible moment.

nutshell-e.text: In a nutshell, the new drug didn't work.

nutshell-l.text: In a nutshell. In a very short summary.

off-chest-e.text: Talking to a counsellor helped her get it off her chest.

off-chest-l.text: Get something off your chest. To talk about something that has been worrying you.

on-the-fence-e.text: You can't sit on the fence forever — we need a decision.

on-the-fence-l.text: Sit on the fence. To avoid choosing between two sides.

on-the-mend-e.text: His speech is improving — he's definitely on the mend.

on-the-mend-l.text: On the mend. Getting better after an illness or injury.

out-of-hand-e.text: The queue in A and E got out of hand during the flu outbreak.

out-of-hand-l.text: Get out of hand. To become impossible to control.

over-moon-e.text: She was over the moon when her paper was accepted.

pain-neck-l.text: A pain in the neck. A person or thing that is very annoying.

piece-of-cake-e.text: After twenty lumbar punctures, the next one was a piece of cake.

piece-of-cake-l.text: A piece of cake. Something very easy to do.

pinch-salt-a.text: Take something with a pinch of salt.

pinch-salt-e.text: Take online reviews with a pinch of salt.

pinch-salt-l.text: Take something with a pinch of salt. Not to believe something completely.

pull-leg-e.text: Relax, I'm just pulling your leg!

pull-leg-l.text: Pull someone's leg. To tell someone something untrue as a joke.

pull-weight-e.text: Everyone on the team has to pull their weight.

pull-weight-l.text: Pull your weight. To do your fair share of the work.

race-time-e.text: Treating a stroke is always a race against time.

race-time-l.text: A race against time. A situation where you must do something very quickly.

round-clock-l.text: Around the clock. All day and all night, without stopping.

same-boat-e.text: Don't worry about the exam — we're all in the same boat.

same-boat-l.text: In the same boat. In the same difficult situation as others.

same-page-e.text: Before we start, let's make sure we're all on the same page.

same-page-l.text: On the same page. Agreeing about what is happening or what to do.

shoestring-e.text: They ran the whole study on a shoestring.

shoestring-l.text: On a shoestring. With very little money.

speak-mind-e.text: At the meeting, feel free to speak your mind.

speak-mind-l.text: Speak your mind. To say honestly what you think.

spill-beans-e.text: Come on, spill the beans — did you get the job?

spill-beans-l.text: Spill the beans. To tell people secret information.

spur-moment-a.text: On the spur of the moment.

spur-moment-e.text: We booked the trip on the spur of the moment.

spur-moment-l.text: On the spur of the moment. Suddenly, without planning.

storm-teacup-e.text: The row about the rota was just a storm in a teacup.

storm-teacup-l.text: A storm in a teacup. A lot of anger or worry about something unimportant.

tighten-belt-e.text: After the cuts, the hospital had to tighten its belt.

tighten-belt-l.text: Tighten your belt. To spend less money.

tip-of-iceberg-e.text: The reported cases are only the tip of the iceberg.

tip-of-iceberg-l.text: The tip of the iceberg. A small, visible part of a much bigger problem.

two-minds-e.text: I'm in two minds about taking the job.

two-minds-l.text: In two minds. Unable to decide between two choices.

up-to-speed-e.text: Can you bring me up to speed on bed twelve?

up-to-speed-l.text: Up to speed. Having the latest information about something.

weather-e.text: I'm feeling a bit under the weather today.

word-mouth-e.text: Most of our patients find us by word of mouth.

word-mouth-l.text: Word of mouth. Information passed from person to person by talking.
